name: S4 rule (spider-nest map separates)
summary: The spider-nest map s₄ — π/4 phase gadgets connecting one input to all 16 subsets of four fresh |+⟩ outputs — disconnects into a ⟨+| effect on the input and four |+⟩ states.
description:
Kissinger and van de Wetering define the *spider-nest maps* $s_n : 1 \to n$ inductively: $s_0$ is a $\frac\pi4$ Z-effect, and $s_n$ copies its input into $s_{n-1}$ and, through an X-spider that also produces the new output, into a second copy of $s_{n-1}$. Unfolded, $s_n$ is the map $\ket{x} \mapsto \sum_{y\in\mathbb F_2^n} \exp\big(\frac{i\pi}4\sum_{S\subseteq[n]} (x\oplus\bigoplus_{i\in S} y_i)\big)\ket{y}$: a $\frac\pi4$ phase gadget on the input together with each of the $2^n$ subsets of the outputs, where the outputs start as $\ket{+}$ states. The *S4 rule* says that $s_4$ *separates*: it equals (up to a scalar) a $\bra{+}$ effect on the input and $\ket{+}$ states on the four outputs, i.e. the total phase does not depend on $x$ or $y$.

Bending the input wire around, this is equivalent to the 5-qubit spider nest in which 16 $\frac\pi4$ gadgets act on qubit 1 together with every subset of qubits 2–5 (Eq. (19) of the paper): its connectivity matrix $(\vec 1\ B_4)$ is triorthogonal. By induction the same holds for every $s_n$ with $n\geq4$. The main result of the paper is that the Clifford ZX-calculus plus this single rule is *diagonally complete* for Clifford+T: it proves every spider nest identity $D_M = I$ (for $M$ triorthogonal), and hence it is complete for CNOT+T circuits. In particular it proves the [4-qubit spider nest](../spider-nest/). It is not complete for all Clifford+T diagrams, since it is sound for an interpretation that breaks [supplementarity](../supplementarity/).
parameter_notes: The paper's rule is the case n = 4. The maps s_n separate for every n ≥ 4 (Lemma 3.3, derived from S4 by induction), but s_n has 2^n gadgets, so these are not offered as a family.

source.location: Section 3, Eq. (18), the S4-rule (the map s_4 of Definition 2.1, Eq. (14))

notes: The paper states the rule in scalable notation, up to a non-zero scalar. Here $s_4$ is unfolded into ordinary ZX: the spider on the left is the input (its $\frac\pi4$ phase is the gadget for the empty subset), the four spiders with outputs are the outputs, and every other spider pair is a $\frac\pi4$ phase gadget connecting the input to a non-empty subset of the outputs.
